L3 is the calculated vertical projection: 1496 − 498 − 25 = 973 mm. The article gives a rough length of about 99 cm. DU1ANV formed the bends around a 12.7 mm jig. After bending, mark the free end for a 25 mm gap (E). The wire length depends on the bends.
The top jumper joins the two radiator legs. The matching stub is shorted at the bottom. Moving both feed contacts along the stub changes the input impedance.

Use insulating spacers to hold the spacing and gap. To match the feed line, move both contacts together in steps of about 5 mm and check SWR. When the resonance was well below the target, DU1ANV shortened the upper radiator while maintaining gap E. Measure SWR and impedance in the final mounting position. The PVC enclosure shifted the author’s result down in frequency. Repeat the sweep after fitting the enclosure or changing the feed line.

M0UKD estimate: λ = c/f, B = kλ/2, C = kλ/4, D = kλ/40, E = λ/100, A = B + C + E. At 145 MHz and k = 0.96, A ≈ 150.93 cm and D ≈ 4.96 cm. Here k is the element shortening factor. The author uses 0.96 for bare copper or aluminium. M0UKD measures between the nearest metal surfaces. DU1ANV’s spacing S is centre to centre.

A 28.500 MHz design using 450-ohm window line. Start with 7.48 m of line. In G0KYA’s drawing, the 6 cm gap starts 2.31 m from the bottom. The initial feed point is 13 cm from the bottom. Adjust it using measurements.

G0KYA · 10 m Slim Jim and scaling notes

λ = c/f, B = kλ/2, C = kλ/4, D = kλ/40, E = λ/100, A = B + C + E. Here k is the element shortening factor. The dimensions use the nearest metal surfaces. Set the conductor spacing to suit the build or the dimensions of the ladder line. D is the initial feed height for adjustment.

The 7.48 m starting blank is based on the OH2EUU build. The cut-out and 13 cm feed height are from the G0KYA drawing. The upper edge is 2.31 + 0.06 = 2.37 m from the bottom. The final height of the G0KYA build is unspecified.
Scale each starting dimension from 28.5 MHz by 28.5 / 51 ≈ 0.559, as suggested by G0KYA. The scaled blank is a starting length. Use the same type of line and adjust the antenna after installation.

λ = c/f. The separate quarter-wave matching line has a physical length L = VF · λ/4. The height comes from the published 20 m build. Use the design drawing for assembly and find the feed taps by measurement.

H is the overall height and L is the length of the separate matching section. 1 — Connect one wire to the longer element and leave the other open. 2 — Short the far end of the line. 3 — Connect the feed through a 1:1 balun at the taps. Diagram not to scale.
Yellow marks the gap and the feed contacts. The centre conductor connects to the continuous leg and the braid to the leg with the gap. Diagram not to scale.
Check SWR and impedance in the final mounting position. Adjust the feed point to suit the actual line and surroundings, then measure again.
Two telescoping aluminium elements joined at the top, with a separate matching section made from 300-ohm twin lead.
The author starts with both feed taps about 1 m (40 in) from the shorted end. Move the taps together to find the lowest SWR on the installed antenna, then secure the connections.
F is the distance between the nearest metal surfaces. Set it to suit the construction or the chosen line.
Slim Jim with integrated matching section. A is the height, B the radiator, C the stub, D the feed height, E the gap and F the clear spacing between conductors.
Slim Jim made from window line. L2 and L2 + E are the heights of the lower and upper cut-out edges from the bottom. E is the gap and h is the feed height.
